OK I tried to create again from the scratch. Well, renaming does not work. Actually everything is well written in plugin Help. Anyway I wrote my own instructions:
File > New Project
Download script: go to Script(Raw) link, then right mouse click and choose Save as... [your project]\js\plugins)
Download babylon.js: go to
http://cdn.babylonjs.com/2-3/babylon.js
, then right mouse click and choose Save as... [your project]\js\libs)
Go to your project folder and open index.html. Make new line after <body style="background-color: black">. Insert into new line "<script type="text/javascript" src="js/libs/babylon.js"></script>]" (without quotes). Save.
Copy tileset rom FPLE MV demo game (the only tileset in FPLE MV Demo\img\tilesets).
Paste tileset in your new project ([your project]\img\tilesets).
Select all the images from FPLE MV Demo\img\textures and copy them to [your project]\img\textures (there is no such folder, so make one before or just copy whole folder from demo).
Open new project and press F9. Choose Tilesets option from left. Then choose first tileset and remove images from A1, A2, A3, B1 etc (all images should be clear - select (None) from list).
Choose image A5 and select tileset FPLE from list.
Choose terrain tag from right and add 1 to tiles that will be your wall tiles. Left some tiles with 0 - it will be your floor tiles.
Shake that... I mean paint that map like it's your last time. Well just paint it.

well you don't want to use the default character sheet and have 400x400 events. that would make the sheet over 6000 pixels in size. You really want to stay below 4096 IMO. For some stuff you just need to get creative. You can't change the textures on walls in the rooms. So design around that. If someone pushes a button and should open a door, either push them through it, or give them an updated message. For example, if there is an axe laying on the ground, don't bake it into the texture. Instead have like a grove or crack or something noticeable like a lever in the texture. Sprites will
always
face the player- they're drawn directly onto the screen like stickers. To make one that has a static facing in the world, you'd need to make it part of a mesh- by which I mean, you'd still have to use the tileset instead of an event. The closest thing you could do would be to make a new 'door' spritesheet that has up/down/left/right, where 'down' is the player facing the door, and left/right are views of the door from the side, or at a very narrow angle? But it would still work pretty awkwardly, sorry.
Normally, it computes which
frame
of the sprite- the "character-facing-left/right/up/down" to use for the sprite based on the relative direction between player and event. If you turned, you'd notice the event seen to change facing right before it went off-camera- now, it keeps the same facing until it's well off camera, unless you've got an FoV of 180 degrees or something. If you use a spritesheet with a ! in the name, it ignores relative direction entirely, and assumes it looks the same from all sides so you can use direction for state changes.
On this note, there's not a good way to update what sprite an event is using at play time either- not without refreshing the map. Try not to rely too much on animation or dynamic maps in general, with this plugin. It has to build a whole 3D scene, and does so mostly when you load the map. Updating things... I might see if there's a nice shortcut, but I suspect trying to update the map at run time could cause performance issues, with how we do it.

posts.author: Doktor_Q
posts.body:
Oh, that's what you meant, sorry. It's probably better to clear things up a bit, to reduce further confusion. Since you're in a 3D space, there's actually two directions:
The direction the event is actually facing, the one you normally use in RPGMaker is the
cardinal direction
. We'll refer to that with north/south/east/west.
After accounting for the camera's position, it calculates the
relative direction
, new to FPLE, which it uses to tell what frame it needs to draw. We'll refer to this with front/back/right/left.
If you have a ! in your filename, FPLE will ignore the relative direction, and always use the cardinal direction to pick the frame
. This is used on things like doors, levers, and the like, because the "direction" is actually the "state" of the object- open/closed, flipped, pressed, etc. Since it
doesn't use the relative direction
, it gives the effect of "always facing the player". There's plenty of reasons you might want to use this- the floating crystals from the default set, camp fires, anything that doesn't change much from various angles.
Removing that quirk requires a bit more effort, because if you look at the image set, it probably only has images from the front. If you remove the !, it would just try to use the various states as directions, and really doesn't have any meaning in the game. Instead, you'll have to make new images! Let's work with the example of a door: Just like making a character, you'll have to make more images of your door for each
relative direction
: You already have the front, now you need to make side and back views of the door.
Now at this point, you've used up all your directions for the sprite to make a closed door. You'll have to make another "character" on the same sprite sheet for each additional state- each one with all four relative directions.
If they aren't on the same sprite sheet, it won't work very well- FPLE doesn't like loading in a new sprite sheet
, but you can change between other sprites on the same sheet.
Lastly, you'll probably want to set the door to Direction Fix so it doesn't face the player when they try open it, and instead of the move route changing directions (as in the Door template event), you need to change the sprite.
Due to the way sprites work, the door will still seem to "turn" very slightly if viewed from an angle, and will always be centered in the tile you place it on. Those are just the limitations of how the FPLE plugin was built, changing them would involve making a new plugin from scratch.

It's pretty limited. RPGMaker was never built to handle 3D, it's a 2D RPG engine, so the fact that it can do this at all is an impressive accomplishment. I don't think I would have had the stamina to build this from the ground up, even with what it could do initially.

posts.author: Doktor_Q
posts.body:
Yes, the ceiling is lifted. In literal code terms: the <room height: > tag gets a height, H. When it builds the map, it places the ceiling blocks at position H+1 (when they're present), and builds walls out of H cubes on top the floor.
As a side effect of building it out of multiple cubes, though, it means your maps count as "too big" more quickly when using a lot of walls. You can mitigate that by never making huge masses of walls, only use them to outline your paths. Not like the player can see through them, anyway.

Well, I haven't gotten any contact from Masked so I tooled up some basic fixes for the sprite sizing / direction problems, applied the 1.5.1-style parameters, and added 4 simple features:
On the event note line, where you put <wall>, you can also put <above> or <below> to position the event where the ceiling or floor would be, respectively.  It might turn into something with more fine control later, but for now it's sufficient to make, for example, an animated floor tile (animated event with <wall> and <below>)
In addition to light radius and light color options, there's an "ambient light" option. Turning it on replaces the character-sourced limited-radius light with a completely even ambient light on every object. You can switch between them by calling the "FPLE setAmbientLight" and "FPLE setCharacterLight" plugin commands.
You can enable sidestep with a parameter, using page up / page down (which are also mapped to q and w), the same buttons you can use to switch actors in most menus.
You can set the turn speed as a parameter. Default is '5', I personally use around 2~3 because turning in place to survey the area before moving is an important part of what I'm making.
Unfortunately I don't know enough about the code as a whole to fix the efficiency yet- it doesn't seem to be caused directly by <wall> events, anyway.

You don't describe what you want very well, but wouldn't something like this be totally independent of the presentation?
I mean, if you want a system where player/enemy attacks each other when they bump into each other, you would just do this with an "event touch" trigger, no matter if the game is presented in 3d or not.
Likewise, if you have something marginally more advanced, the script would not care about the presentation either, since it is fundamentally still a 2d grid based game at the core.
